title: gate-phase-entry.mjs abstains on a tier-restricted row when the tier is undetermined
content: Established by #43 (also closed #45; merged as PR #62, bc67abe on main). BEHAVIOUR NOW LIVE: for a `PREREQUISITES` row that only exists at some tiers (currently only the `1-ba` row, via its `tiers` key), the guard now ABSTAINS (does not apply the row) when `status.risk_tier` is not one of the three known tiers, instead of resolving that absence/malformation to the strictest row and applying it anyway. This is a DELIBERATE reversal of the guard's own general default: `normalizeTier` still resolves an unusable tier to the strictest row for every ORDINARY tiered check, and the header comment in plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs states why the `1-ba` row is the one place that default is wrong -- it is reached at the one checkpoint where the tier is not yet knowable, so 'strictest on unusable' would demand an artifact (`map.json`) that non-architectural tiers are told not to produce. `appliesAtTier(phase, tier, tierDetermined)` takes the RAW `status.risk_tier` (via `tierDetermined = KNOWN_TIERS.includes(status.risk_tier)`) rather than `normalizeTier`'s output, precisely so this abstention cannot be silently defeated by the normalizer coercing an absent/malformed tier into a member of `KNOWN_TIERS` before the check sees it. COST ACCEPTED: the `1-ba` row's `map.json` requirement is RETIRED on the mandated path AT EVERY TIER, not narrowed to architectural, because a row gated on a resolved tier is unreachable at the only visit where the map can still be missing. Re-siting that requirement at a phase where the tier IS resolved is out of scope here and is filed as #61 (which also carries four smaller deferred items as a comment on the issue, per evidence.md's deferring-is-an-action rule: DEV-6 two sites know what a real tier is, DEV-7 a third parameter with no default, a surviving Array.isArray mutation from SecOps, and the 24h in-flight staleness ceiling pinned at neither boundary -- this last one is also independently filed as #63). SECOND COST, accepted explicitly: a typo'd risk_tier now turns a tiers-restricted row OFF rather than ON (fail-open on malformed input, not fail-closed) -- the guard's own header calls this the same shape as `inFlight` refusing to hold a project's turns open on a record it cannot DATE: a record it cannot TIER gets the same treatment, by deliberate analogy, not by borrowed precedent (pipeline-status.mjs's `resolveTier` only supports the ABSENT half of this rule -- it renders absence as `-` but passes a malformed string through verbatim -- so the malformed half is a new judgement made in #43, not inherited). THE SENTENCE THAT TOOK FOUR ATTEMPTS, recorded so the next author does not re-earn this the hard way: the guard needed one sentence stating what `status.risk_tier` IS at the `1-ba` checkpoint, and three earlier phrasings were each falsified by the committed `.pipeline/*/status.json` corpus before the fourth shipped. (1) 'the risk_tier at 1-ba is necessarily absent' -- FALSE at architectural: a rework re-entry re-writes `current_phase: "1-ba"` before EACH BA dispatch (the durable-checkpoint convention), so a record can sit at `1-ba` on a SECOND or later visit with an already-determined tier; this run's own history is the witness (a commit checkpointing `1-ba` for #43 itself while a tier was already set). (2) 'on the FIRST visit to 1-ba the risk_tier is necessarily absent' -- narrowed to dodge (1), still FALSE: Phase 0.5 (`0.5-map`) is itself GATED BY TIER and precedes Phase 1 on the mandated path, and its map dispatch interpolates the tier, so a record whose `0.5-map` has already run reaches its FIRST `1-ba` checkpoint with a tier already in the field. Reviewed against the real corpus (each record's earliest commit whose `current_phase` is `1-ba`): 3 of 4 comparable records carried a tier at that first visit (two architectural experiment records plus this run's own `.pipeline/43`, all having run `0.5-map` first); only `.pipeline/34`, whose `events[]` was empty at that point, had none. So 'on the first visit' was falsified 3-to-1 by the very corpus it was checked against. (3) 'an earlier phase left it there' as the explanation for tier-presence -- also incomplete/misleading on its own: naming rework re-entry as THE cause (as one intermediate draft did) is wrong for the majority shape, since the dominant cause of tier-presence at `1-ba` is a completed `0.5-map` on the ordinary first pass, not rework; and rework is the minority, rarer route to the identical shape. FINAL, SHIPPED WORDING (verified byte-identical across the guard's comment, commands/pipeline.md, and the test's `ANCHOR_43` literal, all three re-derivable with `git grep -rn 'necessarily absent'`, which returns exactly this one surviving paragraph): 'the risk_tier at 1-ba is whatever an EARLIER write left there, never the output of the BA dispatch this checkpoint precedes' -- stated WITHOUT a universal on purpose, because both `(1)` and `(2)` each asserted one and each was falsified. The operative, shape-independent rules that survive regardless of which shape a given record has: a tier that IS present at `1-ba` is read normally (nothing special happens); nothing downstream may infer a tier from its ABSENCE at this phase, or treat an absent tier here as a determined one. RULE LEARNED ON #34, RE-APPLIED HERE: a FIRES cell in a mutation/control assertion may rest on the live corpus, because a corpus can only grow and a FIRES cell only needs at least one qualifying record to exist forever after. A SILENCE cell may NOT rest on the live corpus, because any newly committed record can break it (exactly what happened on #34, where a live-corpus SILENCE assertion broke the moment a new record supplied the counterexample). This run's own coupling/anchor tests (`#43-K1`/`#43-K2`/`#43-K3` in tests/test-gate-phase-entry.sh) were built following that split: the FIRES-shaped assertions stayed anchored to the real `.pipeline/*/status.json` corpus, while the SILENCE-shaped ones (e.g. 'no earlier wording survives') were moved onto crafted trees or scoped to exact-string greps precisely so a future committed record cannot silently invalidate them. MEASURED COST for comparison against future runs of similar shape: `review_rounds: 4` (two Phase 2 specification rounds -- SecOps blocked round 1 on the retire-at-every-tier scope point, cleared round 2 -- plus two Phase 4 panel rounds -- QA blocked round 1 on the anchor's false universal, cleared after a delta re-review of qa/secops/ba/dba), a six-role Phase 4 panel (ba, dba, devops, secops, dev, qa), three fix rounds total across both phases, and the suite assertion count moved 2071 (post-#34 baseline) -> 2216 on main at merge (bc67abe). Contrast: #39, a related phase-vocabulary-rot issue, took seven review rounds -- #43 in 4 is comparatively cheap despite needing four attempts at one sentence.
